page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 186.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, the instance bundles two NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs, delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. No local storage is included, meaning all storage must be network-attached. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1104.08 and a poor single-threaded gzip compression rate of 19.19 GB/sec. However, the instance scales effectively in multi-threaded tasks, achieving an average multi-core stress-ng score of 35393.62 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 149.01 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains steady in the middle tier, measuring 98.26 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 44.08 GB/sec for write operations. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 33.17 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 22.34 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c24g1.12xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the premium cost of newer-generation hardware. The combination of 48 dedicated cores and dual NVIDIA T4 GPUs makes this instance suitable for parallel processing tasks, machine learning inference, video transcoding, and multi-threaded data processing. However, the weak single-core performance and lack of local storage represent key tradeoffs, making it less suitable for single-threaded applications or workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O.
